name: Forty Floors and a Waiver (The Ascent Games Collapse)
creator: Anonymous attendee neural capture; viral spread via RED STATIC collective
description: In 2215, Axiom's 'Ascent Games' — a heavily marketed Tier 2-3 gamified corporate loyalty event held in a 40-floor vertical mall — ended when the event's proprietary BCI integration software caused all 2,300 participants to simultaneously receive achievement notifications for a level called 'FLOOR 41' in a building with 40 floors. The resulting mass confusion, with thousands of people checking exits and stairwells for a nonexistent floor while Axiom staff insisted it was 'part of the experience,' was captured in dozens of simultaneous neural feeds. The phrase 'looking for floor 41' now means chasing something a corporation told you exists.
medium: neural feed multi-capture, audio, BCI notification screenshot
cultural_impact: The event crystallized widespread anxiety about BCI-mediated reality in corporate contexts — if your interface tells you there's a Floor 41, how do you know there isn't? The phrase is used for any pursuit of a promised reward that doesn't exist.
controversy: Axiom maintained until 2017 that Floor 41 was 'a conceptual space representing limitless potential'; the class action suit was settled for undisclosed compensation and participants were required to delete their neural captures, which they did not.
story_hooks: A character has a neural capture from the event that clearly shows an Axiom employee who knew exactly what was happening and said nothing.
Someone claims there actually was a Floor 41 — a sealed corporate level — and the software error exposed its existence accidentally.
The lead developer of the integration software disappeared from Axiom's public employee registry six weeks after the event.
